newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends sharply lower on USDA acreage data.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends sharply lower on USDA acreage data.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter closed sharply down after earlier slipping to its lowest level in almost three years, depressed by the continued improvement in the outlook for this year's U.S. crops.
Dealers noted the U.S. Department of Agriculture increased acreage estimates for both winter and spring wheat while there was also talk the yield outlook for both crops was improving.
"They not only revised spring wheat acreage up but they also revised winter wheat acreage up. Everyone is also feeling the (wheat) crop is in better shape that it ever has been," one dealer said.

USDA put winter wheat harvested acreage at 41.58 million acres, up from its previous projection of 40.85 million, with substantial upward revisions in key hard red states Oklahoma (5.40 million from 5.00 million) and Texas (4.1 million from 3.7 million).
Spring wheat acreage was estimated by USDA at 19.2 million acres, above all estimates which ranged 17.6- million to 18.8-million acres in a Reuter survey of analysts.
Dealers said recent rains had improved the outlook for spring wheat while reports from hard red winter wheat areas also suggested yields were higher than had been expected.
July wheat slipped to a contract low of $3.30-1/2 a bushel, the lowest level for the nearby month since July 1994. It closed off 8-1/2 cents at $3.30-3/4.
Other months were down 6-1/2 to 3-1/2 cents.
